headline: Maclane Started A Quarterback Who Was Ruled Out. His $2 Bench Back Scored 34.6.
kicker: (Lamar Jackson: 0.00. Aaron Rodgers on the bench. 67.9 percent, the worst lineup of the season. The best one scores 158.68.)
lede: Maclane started Lamar Jackson, who was ruled out, and got 0.00 from the quarterback slot with Aaron Rodgers on the bench. Tyler Allgeier, a $2 auction buy, ran for 147 yards and two touchdowns on that bench: 34.6. Kenny Gainwell added 16.0 next to him. On Sunday morning Maclane picked up the Lions, started them for 10.42 and benched the Vikings, who scored 10.44. 50.90 points of regret, 67.9 percent, the worst lineup anyone has played this season. His best lineup was the second-highest score of the week. He went 0-2. Elsewhere: Chris is 16-0. Barrett scored 160.90 and beat everybody. Joe Burrow scored 44.48 for Will, the best start of the season, and snapped a five-game losing streak. Jon played his first perfect lineup of the year and went 0-2 with it. Anuj is on a winning streak.

sections.awards: Fourteen citations. One quarterback who never played, one who threw five touchdowns, and a defense swap decided by two cents.
sections.power: Season to date: record, points, all-play and this week's form, weighted, with movement from last week. Best lineup is the record each team would own if it had started its best legal lineup every week, everyone else exactly as they played. The tax is the difference: wins left on your own bench.
sections.median: Week 8's line was 111.06, the lowest of the season. Anuj cleared it by 1.54. Jon missed it by 1.54 with a perfect lineup. Greg (IR) lost his game and got a win here; Nishil won his and lost here. Right of the line is a win.
sections.standings: Week 8 scoring, both results, and how much of your own roster you managed to start. Efficiency is what you scored over what your best legal lineup would have scored. Injured reserve does not count against you. Four teams hit 100.0 percent. Two went 2-0, two went 0-2.
sections.bench: 158.90 points of lineup regret this week, up from 125.46. Maclane accounts for 50.90 of it by himself, starting with a quarterback who was ruled out.
sections.faab: Every dollar of Week 8, audited. $29 spent, 33 adds, the quietest week since Week 1. Darrius spent $10 and got 37.62 points. Tom spent $12 on a tight end who scored 6.5.
sections.money: Auction dollars against everything each player has scored so far, started or not. A.J. Brown: $45, 14.6 points in eight weeks.
sections.studs: The best and worst starts of Week 8, measured against what Yahoo thought they would do. Lamar Jackson is not on this list because Yahoo projected him for zero. Maclane did not.
sections.games: The long version, closest game first.

games.note: Anuj won again. Two straight after 0-6, and his first 2-0 week of the season: he cleared the median by 1.54, the smallest margin on the right side of the line. Dak Prescott scored 19.8, Bucky Irving 23.0. Then the Emmett Johnson file, now three entries long. Week 6: started, 5.4. Week 7: benched, 6.94. Week 8: benched, 128 receiving yards, 26.06. Anuj's regret this week was 26.06 points, all of it Emmett. Tre Tucker started at receiver and scored 0.00. Jon played his first perfect lineup of the season, 100.0 percent, 109.52, and it was the eighth score in the league: missed the median by 1.54, lost by 3.08, 0-2. Bo Nix over Deshaun Watson, 19.28 to 11.16, the right quarterback three weeks running. Bijan Robinson ($69) scored 7.6, Chris Godwin 0.00. A.J. Brown was on bye: 14.6 points in eight weeks for $45, $3.08 a point, exactly the margin Jon lost by. 3-13, four straight.

Nishil won his second straight head-to-head game and still went 1-1, the only team the median sunk this week, by 4.48. Omar Cooper ($16), 21.0 last week, started and scored 0.00. Makai Lemon, benched last Monday the night he scored 16.2, started this week and scored 8.7. Jaydon Blue, a Wednesday pickup, scored 8.16 on the bench. Alex Singleton held the IDP slot again, 13.0. Abhishek played a perfect lineup, 100.0 percent, 96.80. It was perfect because five of his bench players were on bye: Nico Collins, Isaiah Likely, Tank Dell, Mike Evans and Ka'imi Fairbairn, zero each. He made six adds and started all six: Chig Okonkwo ($0) 2.2, Chad Ryland ($0) 10.9, the Falcons 6.7, Savion Williams 2.8, Elic Ayomanor 4.9 and Treylon Burks, added at 1:19 on Sunday, 9.6. 37.1 points from six transactions. Last week he lost to the 1-11 team. This week he lost to the 3-11 team. 2-11 in all-play.

Darrius spent $10 on Tuesday night and both bids started. Malik Willis ($5) scored 15.64 at quarterback. The Jaguars ($5) scored a touchdown and 21.98. Tyler Goodson, a Friday pickup, scored 9.46 and Michael Wilson ($8) 23.8. Then the Keenan Allen Experience, season two: benched for 7.0, benched for 12.2, started for 5.6, benched this week for 10.2. Parker Washington scored 3.1 in the flex spot Keenan would have had. 2-0 anyway, up three to third, at 8-8. Greg (IR) had Brock Purdy on bye, so he started Jacoby Brissett, the quarterback he benched for 16.48 last week. Brissett threw for 119 yards and an interception: 4.46 on a 19.11 projection. Zay Flowers started and scored 0.00. Bhayshul Tuten scored 29.9 and Jonah Coleman 18.4, and the median saved Greg by 21.46, so 1-1. Five straight head-to-head losses. Dylan Sampson scored 11.86 on the bench. 38 moves.

Andrew finally started Kyle Pitts. Pitts had scored 12.7, 20.5 and 10.7 on the bench in his last three weeks. In the lineup: two catches, six yards, 1.6. Harold Fannin scored 20.4 on the bench behind him. Chris Rodriguez, a $2 waiver claim, scored 12.3 on the bench too. On Saturday afternoon Andrew added Ja'Kobi Lane at 12:40, Justice Hill at 1:34 and Corey Kiner at 5:13. Lane was gone before kickoff; Hill (5.5) and Kiner (3.8) watched from the bench. Antonio Williams, the receiver he added twice during Washington's bye, started this week and scored 7.9. 81.7 percent, won by 20.90, 2-0. Maclane started Lamar Jackson, who was ruled out: 0.00, with Aaron Rodgers on the bench. Tyler Allgeier ($2) scored 34.6 on the bench and Kenny Gainwell 16.0, while Jonathan Taylor ($62) started for 4.7 and Keon Coleman for 0.9 at flex. Lions picked up Sunday at 8:09 AM and started for 10.42; Vikings benched for 10.44. Tee Higgins scored 34.5 and it was not close. 67.9 percent, the worst lineup of the season. The best one scores 158.68, beats Andrew by 30 and clears the median by 47.62. Maclane missed it by 3.28.

Joe Burrow threw for 462 yards and five touchdowns and ran for another: 44.48, the best start by anyone this season. Ja'Marr Chase added 27.6. Matthew Stafford scored 9.28 on the bench, the right quarterback for the second week running. 155.46, 12-1 in all-play, won by 47.34. Will's five-game head-to-head losing streak is over. The Jets defense scored 2.76, after 3.7 last week, and is still starting. Greg (Miley) had three straight perfect lineups. This week: Jared Goff started for 10.04, Bryce Young scored 12.36 on the bench, 95.3 percent, streak over. Javonte Williams, 155 rushing yards last week, ran for 56: 6.2. Cam Skattebo was on bye. Missed the median by 2.94, 0-2, down two.

16-0. Eight head-to-head wins, eight median wins, and Chris played his first perfect lineup of the season to make sure. He started four players he added this week: the Commanders (15.42) and Foyesade Oluokun (9.0), both added Wednesday at 11:26, Marvin Mims (7.7), added Thursday night, and Greg Dulcich, added at 1:43 on Sunday afternoon, 6.3 at tight end. Tony Pollard scored 28.2, Josh Allen 27.56, Jahmyr Gibbs 25.8. $95 of FAAB left, $5 spent all season. Tom scored 93.10, the league low, 0-13 in all-play. Last week he started Kyler Murray over Patrick Mahomes and was right by 6.90. This week, same call: Kyler 20.9, Mahomes 25.44 on the bench. Brenton Strange cost $12, the biggest bid of the week, and scored 6.5 at flex. AJ Barner, added at 1:08 on Sunday, scored 3.3 at the other flex. Drake London ($45): 3.3. Lost by 53.48. The house is 0-2 for the second straight week.

Barrett scored 160.90, the high score of the week, 13-0 in all-play, and played his first perfect lineup of the season. Brock Bowers caught two touchdowns, 24.7. Braelon Allen ($1) scored 23.3. Jordan Love ($2) threw three, 22.52, and has 155.84 points this season, the best value in the league. 8-0 against the median, best-lineup record 16-0, won by 64.72, the biggest margin of the week. Nathan benched Kirk Cousins for Jayden Daniels, back from his bye. Cousins: three touchdown passes and a rushing touchdown, 28.18, on the bench. Daniels: 14.98. CeeDee Lamb scored 9.3, Quinshon Judkins 5.9. 96.18, 1-12 in all-play, 0-2. Yahoo also went back and gave Fred Warner a tackle and a forced fumble from Week 7, so Nathan's perfect lineup that week now wins by 4.12. Nice for him. This week it does not help.
